title: Nimsdai: Lost on Broad Peak
excerpt: Legendary climber Nirmal "Nimsdai" Purja, hero of the Netflix film 14 Peaks and holder of a record 57 ascents above 8,000 meters, died in a Broad Peak avalanche along with nine other climbers.
seoTitle: Nimsdai Purja Dies in Broad Peak Avalanche: The Man Behind the Records

content.value: On 30 July 2026, around nine in the morning, a massive avalanche swept down the main gully of Broad Peak, the twelfth highest mountain in the world. It carried ten climbers with it. Among the dead was Nirmal Purja, known worldwide as "Nimsdai", one of the greatest climbers history has ever seen.

In a single moment, the global mountaineering community lost a man who turned the word "impossible" into something worth checking twice. This is the story of the man behind the records, and of the day the mountain exacted its heaviest price.
Who was Nirmal "Nimsdai" Purja

Nirmal Purja was born in Nepal and left his homeland young to join the British Armed Forces. He served in the Gurkhas, and later became one of the first Nepalis accepted into the Special Boat Service, the elite unit of the British Navy.

Years of service in extreme conditions, hostile environments and constant pressure built in him a rare ability to function in places where the human body is simply meant to shut down. Those skills would later become the foundation of his life's project.
In 2019 he retired from military service and set out on the journey that would make him a legend.

content.caption: The Annapurna massif in Nepal, the first 8,000-meter peak Nimsdai summited on his journey · Photo: Bijay Chaurasia

content.value: Project Possible: 14 peaks in six months
There are 14 peaks in the world above 8,000 meters. Before Nimsdai, climbing all 14 took the fastest mountaineers years, sometimes an entire decade.
Nimsdai declared a goal that sounded absurd: to summit all 14 in less than seven months. The project was named Project Possible.

On 23 April 2019 he stood on the summit of Annapurna, the first of the journey. Six months and six days later, on 29 October 2019, he stood on Shishapangma and completed the mission. It was a record experts believed would only fall in decades, if ever, and it still stands today.
The film that made him a global name

In 2021 his story became a Netflix documentary, 14 Peaks: Nothing Is Impossible. The film chronicled the entire project, from bureaucratic obstacles and extreme cold to human moments such as rescuing other climbers mid-expedition.

The film became an instant global hit and drew wide acclaim. It transformed Nimsdai from a figure known within the climbing community into an international cultural star, and a source of inspiration for millions, especially for people from developing nations who saw in him living proof that even the biggest dream can be reached.
His 57th summit, nine days before the disaster
Since completing Project Possible, Nimsdai never stopped climbing. He kept collecting 8,000-meter peaks, each time pushing a little further at what was considered possible.

On 21 July 2026, just nine days before the disaster, he summited Gasherbrum II at 8,035 meters. It was his 57th ascent above 8,000 meters, and he did it without supplemental oxygen, his 29th time without oxygen.

content.title: ✦ A record
content.value: 57 summits above 8,000 meters, more than any other climber in history. 29 of them without supplemental oxygen.
With those numbers, Nimsdai became the climber with the most eight-thousander summits ever. And then he decided to keep going a little further.
The final mission, cut short

In 2026 Nimsdai announced a new project: to climb all 14 eight-thousanders three times over, while also completing the Seven Summits, the highest peak on each continent, three times. All without supplemental oxygen.
In a post he shared before leaving for Broad Peak, he wrote:

"This was not the original plan. I only meant to climb Gasherbrum II. But right before leaving for Pakistan I counted my 8,000ers again, and it hit me: if I also climb Broad Peak while I am here, only Cho Oyu remains for me to become the first person in history to climb all 14 eight-thousanders twice. Without oxygen."
The journey meant to complete half of that ambitious project ended in tragedy.
What happened on Broad Peak

Broad Peak, at 8,047 meters, is the twelfth highest mountain in the world. It stands in the Karakoram range in Pakistan, near K2, and is considered one of the less technically demanding eight-thousanders. Less demanding, but far from safe.

In the weeks before the disaster, heavy snow fell on the Karakoram. Other expeditions at base camp chose to evacuate and go home because of the risk. Climbers who left the mountain described how Broad Peak had "changed its mood" dramatically. Nimsdai's team chose to stay.

On 30 July, in the morning hours, a massive avalanche swept down the main gully and carried all ten members of the team, who were moving between camps two and three at around 6,500 meters. Contact with them was lost at once.

Pakistani army rescue teams went into action, but harsh weather and extreme terrain slowed the operation. Over the following days the bodies of the victims were gradually located and recovered. None of the ten team members survived.

content.caption: The high Himalaya, a world where the summit always exacts a price

content.value: Ten climbers, one global family
The team that perished numbered ten, climbers and Sherpa guides from Nepal, the United States, Oman, Pakistan and China. Their names:

items: Nirmal "Nimsdai" Purja (Nepal and the UK), expedition leader.
Nadhira Al-Harthy (Oman), the first woman from her country to summit Everest.
Sarah Mallory Geis (United States), a 39-year-old climber from Texas who closed her studio to chase her mountain dream.
Pur Bahadur "Yukta" Gurung (Nepal), a veteran high-altitude guide.

content.value: Each of them carried a story, a dream, and a family waiting at home.
The meeting at Manaslu Base Camp
For the HighAir team, this disaster feels closer than usual. In September 2025, one of HighAir's founders was at Manaslu Base Camp with one of our expeditions, and met Nimsdai himself.

The photo of the two of them at base camp, less than a year before the disaster, turned in an instant from the memory of a professional encounter into part of the legacy of a legend lost. What stayed with us is a man who was exactly as we had hoped: warm, present, and full of an energy that touched everyone who stood beside him.
The real risks of high-altitude climbing
The Broad Peak avalanche is a painful reminder that even the most experienced climbers in the world face real risks on the high mountains. These are the main dangers every climber must know:

items: Avalanches: the greatest danger on high mountains. Fresh snow over an unstable base creates ideal conditions for a slide.
Altitude sickness: above 3,000 meters the risk rises sharply. The 8,000-meter peaks sit in the "death zone", an altitude where the human body cannot recover.
Weather changes: at great height a storm can break in under an hour. Good weather windows are short and unpredictable.
Glaciers and crevasses: high-altitude glaciers constantly shift and split, creating the risk of falling into deep crevasses.
Mental strain: at altitude, decision-making becomes harder, and many climbers push for the summit despite warning signs because of their emotional investment.

content.value: This is exactly why high-altitude climbing demands thorough preparation, professional guidance, and absolute respect for the warnings the mountain gives.

content.value: A legacy of inspiration
Nirmal Purja was not only a climber. He was a symbol of possibility, living proof that a person of humble origins can reach heights no one dared to dream of.

Beyond his personal achievements, Nimsdai founded the Nimsdai Foundation, which funded social projects in Nepal. One of the most notable was the porter house in Lobuche, a center providing shelter for porters in the Everest region, part of his fight for the rights of Nepal's high-altitude workers.

He was a strong, clear voice on the need to recognize the contribution of local Sherpas and porters, the people who so often remain anonymous beside the famous Western climbers. In that too, he changed the game.
Frequently asked questions
Who was Nirmal "Nimsdai" Purja?

A Nepali-British climber regarded as one of the greatest in history. He was the first person in the world to summit all 14 peaks above 8,000 meters in under seven months, a record that still stands today.
How did Nimsdai Purja die?
He died along with nine other climbers in an avalanche on Broad Peak in Pakistan, on 30 July 2026. None of the ten team members survived.
What is the Netflix film 14 Peaks?
14 Peaks: Nothing Is Impossible is a 2021 Netflix documentary chronicling Project Possible, Nimsdai's ascent of all 14 peaks above 8,000 meters in under seven months.
Where is Broad Peak?
Broad Peak, at 8,047 meters, sits in the Karakoram range on the border between Pakistan and China, near K2. It is the twelfth highest mountain in the world.
How many climbers died in the Broad Peak avalanche?
In the avalanche on 30 July 2026, all ten members of the team died: climbers and Sherpa guides from Nepal, the United States, Oman, Pakistan and China.
